title: LOW-VALUES (0x00) and HIGH-VALUES (0xFF) — used as sentinels in sort/merge keys; not 'empty string'
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SORT-MARKER.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> LOW-VALUES = all 0x00 bytes. Sorts FIRST in collating order.
      *> HIGH-VALUES = all 0xFF bytes. Sorts LAST.
      *> Code that MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO WS-KEY is creating an
      *> end-of-table marker. Java's empty string "" sorts to a
      *> totally different place and breaks the SORT key.
       01  WS-KEY    PIC X(10).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO WS-KEY.
           STOP RUN.
notes: LOW-VALUES / HIGH-VALUES are not 'null' or 'empty' — they're specific byte patterns chosen for their position in the EBCDIC/ASCII collating order. The spec must capture their use as sentinels so the rewrite picks an appropriate target (e.g. Character.MIN_VALUE).
